quotes.excerpt: Seven issues in, End of Life continues to prove why it is one of the best comics of the year with its frantic energy, nihilistic humour and stylised artwork. This series keeps finding new ways to make the scenarios stranger and the characters even angrier at Eddie, all of them weaving in and out to create a truly chaotic yet entertaining story.

I know I sound like a broken record but I can’t stop singing this comic run its praises! Kyle Starks makes someone as unlikeable as Eddie Stallion a character you want to root for, and brings a compelling story along with him. This comic is a full course meal and only gets better and better.
Power Rangers Unlimited #1 is a bold, legacy embracing start which easily grabs hold of the best of BOOM!-era Power Rangers comics and presents it from a fresh and exciting angle.

Power Rangers Unlimited #1 delivers an action-packed debut that leans into Power Rangers history from a fresh point of view, and when combined with the out-of-this-world art and extensive roster, Power Rangers Unlimited becomes a must-read for any and every fan of the franchise.
This was a great issue finally getting Superman in front of Kryl-Ux and getting us ready for the battle. I really like Superman in this issue, trying to help. Plus, a Supergirl sighting!

The legacy of the Warworld Saga reaches far and wide in this series, and that’s why I personally think it’s the best Superman story of the last decade. Hopefully Johnson’s whole epic run gets an omnibus.

True crime fans looking for something unusual will be in hog heaven. So will fans of the Minor Threats series, which features a similarly genre-bending level of fun. In fact, I dare say everyone should visit Witness Point.

Witness Point #1 succeeds because it understands that a great crime story needs more than a clever premise. Nathan Fillon and Heath Corson build a small town full of personalities, grudges, secrets, and simmering tension, while artist Soo Lee gives every character enough individuality to make them feel like a suspect, a victim, or both. The witness protection angle provides an irresistible foundation, but the issue never relies solely on its elevator pitch. Instead, it carefully constructs a mystery populated by colorful characters, sharp dialogue, and just enough chaos, including a tiger attack, to keep readers on their toes. If the series can maintain this level of plotting and characterization, Witness Point has all the ingredients to become one of the year's standout crime comics.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

This is a ripping yard of piracy and sorcery, which highlights an often overlooked aspect of Conan’s background and the true character of Valeria of the Red Brotherhood. The artwork holds to the same standard of detail and drive. If you think of Conan as little more than a big, dumb barbarian, prepare to be educated!

Ultimately, A Mischief of Magpies is a haunting and beautiful book that goes far beyond merely being simply a solid fantasy. It’s an immersive story that resonates on so many levels. There’s a magic to this book that will break your heart—and it might be one of the best books to come out this year.
A Mischief Of Magpies #1 is perfection and sticks out as one of the best comics of the year so far. A must get.

Killer Influences #1 stands out by blending societies true crime obsession with influencer culture in a way that feels both unsettling and original. Joey Esposito crafts a chilling tale, while Valeria Burzo and Iñaki Azpiazu really bring the story together with excellent illustrations and color. Killer Influences is a gripping true crime story turning fame and fear into a dangerously addictive pact.

All in all, fans of dark comedy and true crime will find Killer Influences bloody hilarious. More sensitive souls need not apply. However, if you’re a fan of Only Murders in the Building, this will be up your alley.
Queen In Black: Venom Unchained Issue 1 is a terrific change of pace from the other tie-ins and Queen in Black main book.
As tremendous a story from Charles Soule together with spectacular artwork make this an issue you do NOT want to miss out on!
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

The story is great, the art is stunning, and it’s a trial by fire for Superboy Prime that makes me more confident than ever that this character is actually here to stay. Just an amazing turnaround for this once-hated figure.

Superman #39 is a can’t-miss issue for this Spring’s biggest event. This issue sets up exciting new things for the DC Universe. This is an all-star creative team, and it feels like they are not holding back their talents at all with this arc.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!
Power Rangers Unlimited #1 is a bold, legacy embracing start which easily grabs hold of the best of BOOM!-era Power Rangers comics and presents it from a fresh and exciting angle.

Power Rangers Unlimited #1 delivers an action-packed debut that leans into Power Rangers history from a fresh point of view, and when combined with the out-of-this-world art and extensive roster, Power Rangers Unlimited becomes a must-read for any and every fan of the franchise.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

We get our first hints of how this fits in with the rest of the Absolute Universe just as it ends, but this feels much more like an evergreen, one-of-a-kind comic that people will be talking about for years.

Camp, Rodríguez and Otsmane-Elhaou leave readers with an intense read unlike anything else seen in the comics landscape currently. A phenomenal script gels perfectly with Rodríguez’s incredible art yet again. While its’ a bittersweet moment with the series on hold/over, readers leave with an overwhelming sense of the true direction of superhero comics for years to come. Highest possible recommendation.
Superman: The Stranger #1 returns to Clark Kent's roots, spinning a story that shows why Superman is such a timeless character.

The best Superman comic I’ve read in years!  A 1930s reinvention of the Man of Steel that returns Superman to his 1930s roots, but zigs and zags in ways you won’t expect, while keeping you on your toes. With a story that hooks you from the go and art and colours that leap off the page, this is a must-read mini-series.

Even with the set up happening in a different series, Detective Comics #1113 is such a near perfect Batman adventure that it could convince even the most cash-strapped bat-fans to add it to their pulls.

Batman takes to the skies to save his city in a thrilling addition to “Bad Seeds”! Taylor throws a daring rescue attempt in Bat’s direction with great success. Spokes jumps in and keeps the excitement running high all issue long. In Gotham’s darkest hour, Batman is still bringing the fight in its’ honor.

The Finest meet the Harbingers in a great opening round of the latest arc! Waid crafts the dangerous plans of Al Ghul with a magnificent start. Gutiérrez & the team deliver a thrilling journey into the fight for survival. World’s Finest is always a safe bet to deliver each time out!

Batman/Superman: World’s Finest #55 launches its new arc with the huge superhero spectacle this series does so well. Mark Waid wastes little time establishing Ra’s al Ghul’s terrifying plan, while Adrián Gutiérrez keeps the action fast, inventive, and appropriately dangerous. The villain team-up adds an unpredictable element, and the rapidly escalating global threat gives this opening chapter the scale of a full-blown event.
Catwoman #91 brings empathy and a heist to the Bad Seeds event making for an intriguing angle as the stories slowly set up to converge!
Catwoman #91 ties the series into Batman: Bad Seeds in an organic, compelling way while also providing moments of genuine character growth.

King’s plot has been long and winding. The overarching story that's taken so long to reach this particular point has been spotty at best. There are occasional issues that feel very weak and occasional treatments of classic ideas that also feel very weak. However, the overall story that King is jamming into place begins to feel like a little bit more of an accomplishment with each issue. It hasn't exactly been a graceful journey. However, it does begin to feel like.King is going to be able to tell a compelling story featuring Wonder Woman that continues t hrough her 85th birthday next month.
Wonder Woman #37 expertly balances foreshadowing and top notch action to deliver a blockbuster beginning to the second part of the "Wonder War" story arc.

I’ll sound like a broken record but if you haven’t dived into this run, what are you waiting for?! Every arc is somehow better than the last. The character’s development is making huge changes that’ll go down in X-Men history. The stories will have you hooked onto every page. Plus, the creative team makes this entire issue a feast for the eyes. The Uncanny X-Men #35 continues that impossibly high quality that we’re so used to seeing in this run.

The demons within strike Rogue and Gambit as his curse worsens in this latest chapter! Simone locks in on their struggles while staging Howler’s storyline in a new direction. Vecchio and Wilson deliver a showcase of action and drama between the panels. This series keeps redefining what X-Men stories should be!

This new story arc for the TMNT Universe is proving to be a challenge that they were warned would happen. I can understand wanting both of your parents back, but at the cost of New York City… This team continues to produce amazing issues every month with great action and storytelling. The added Chinese lore to this series is a joy to see. Seeing the Turtles engage in their heritage is something people should mimic. Take pride in your roots and where you come from. This is a great series and a great read for TMNT and non-TMNT fans.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #22 delivers an exciting escalation of The City That Never Dies, combining supernatural mystery, family consequences, and clear, atmospheric artwork. Gene Luen Yang, Fero Pe, and Luis Antonio Delgado turn Obon into the backdrop for a compelling catastrophe, leaving the Turtles facing a larger and more personal threat. It is a strong, fast-moving issue that builds anticipation for what comes next.

New Titans #39 further stokes the fires of conflict as the Titans race to help Wonder Girl's people, leading to tense character moments. With the Esquecidas in danger, the Titans will have to pull it together, but the question remains: can they finally become a team?

A trip to Akahim becomes more than the team is ready to handle with this latest chapter. Brombal lets Flor get the lead role with a solid script. The art team showcases the underlying drama while addressing the monsters in the vicinity. A curious tale that has much room to expand its’ impressions with.

A great issue that is one of the best issues of the year. Jed MacKay pens an incredibly compelling issue that will make you want to re-read the issue again. Together with stunning artwork, this is an issue you can’t pass up on.

X-Men #37 builds on a key plot point from DNX, displaying a psychic war in all of its glory. It also sets the stage for the future of Mackay's run, and that future might involve more of what X-Men fans have been wanting to see.
I wish I could give this 11/10 but alas, Redcoat #20 is violent, rage fueled, and satisfying all at the same time. It’s cowardly Simon Pure in a way we have never seen him before.

Redcoat #20 is a raw, relentless issue that turns Simon’s grief into a deeply personal battle for revenge. Geoff Johns keeps the story emotionally focused, while the art team makes every blow feel brutal and consequential. The result is a visually powerful, emotionally charged issue that delivers one of the series’ most intense confrontations. If you are looking for an emotional, action-packed ride this is the issue for you. Grab a copy at your LCS this week and enjoy the violence.

More secrets revealed, more dangers unlocked. Pichetshote keeps the intensity up as Dinah processes what’s she’s learned. Albuquerque & Maiolo unleash a furious display of action amongst the heavy drama. An exceptional journey into the moral compass of justice.

Absolute Green Arrow #5 is a major step up as Pornsak Pichetshote delivers answers, expands the conspiracy, and brings the series' grotesque horror roaring back. The reveal of the masked Green Arrow gives Merlyn considerably more depth, while his history with Ollie makes the larger fight against the ultra-wealthy feel more personal. Rafael Albuquerque and Adriano Lucas Maiolo make the monsters appropriately disturbing, with a few unforgettable images that give this chapter real bite.

G.I. Joe #26 is an all-out action showcase, delivering a blockbuster G.I. Joe vs. Night Force showdown while Tom Reilly fills every page with spectacular combat and the story quietly sets up what comes next.

Night Force goes for the knockout but Duke never hears the bell in this action packed issue! Williamson delivers an exciting showdown with huge ramifications. Is anyone doing better action art than Tom Reilly and the team? Look at the high-octane panels on display here! There’s no better action series on the market right now than G.I. Joe!

Superman Unlimited #17 is a fast-paced issue that puts Superman’s golden powers at the forefront in a race to save the world. As we near the end of the “Kingdom of Zod” event, there’s only one obstacle remaining and that’s Zod himself (or at least a younger version of him).

Superman Unlimited #17 is a testament to the Man of Steel's everlasting spirit, as the "Kingdom of Zod" storyline rockets to its end. The Kryptonite threat might be over, but the shadow of Zod still looms.

reason.snippet: Sleepy Hollow: The Witches of Western Wood #5 ends Sarah Archer's tale in a tide of blood, revenge, and shattered family bonds.
pros: Jaro fills each page with disturbing imagery, most notably a row of severed heads.
Horchar's color art drenches whole pages in shadows, slowly letting in light and revealing the horrors within.
Dawson's script highlights the true horror of this miniseries, which is Sarah's refusal to let her sister go.
A perfect read for fans of Sleepy Hollow or those who want to get in the Halloween spirit.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Gargoyles #2 is a sophomore issue packed with moments big and small, but the small ones stand out most. The creative team should definitely keep that in mind for future issues.
pros: The small character moments are the best in this issue.
Gambone and Bevard perfectly captures the mix of moodiness and myth that defines Gargoyles.
Weisman excels when scripting Brooklyn and Katana's clash against Coldstone.
cons: The comic feels a bit overloaded in terms of plot.

reason.snippet: Marc Spector: Moon Knight #8 might take place in the dark, but it's layered with shades of gray as the creative team reminds readers that Marc Spector is a deeply flawed man.
pros: MacKay doesn't shy away from showcasing that Spector is a flawed man, and how that impacts his relationships.
Pramanik shifts from horror to action with ridiculous ease.
Rosenberg's use of colors will lead to some chilling imagery.
Clea turns out to be the MVP of the entire issue.

This issue feels a bit like a filler issue and feels like there could have been more than happened with the Jeff Coast Avengers. Kelly Thompson finds a way to write scenes commonly found in other media into comics in a way that feels natural. Tokitokoro and Jim Ca…
pros: Kelly Thompson writes another amazing scene which borrows from popular scenes in other media.
Tokitokoro and Jim Campbell's art is unique and immerses you into the montage scene.
cons: This issue make you aware of how much time has passed and it makes the issue feel short.
It feels like not enough happened with the Jeff Coast Avengers.

pros: DaNi and Matt Hollingsworth’s artistic collaboration perfectly invokes the dark and gritty tone of the Batman: Bad Seeds event
Cliffhanger ending sets up what is sure to be a thrilling battle between Batwoman and the TUCOS next issue

The story leans heavily on familiar gang…
